t: You're in Bryanston Square, an 800-by-200-foot garden square in Marylebone, surrounded by terraced buildings, some still residential. At the southern end is the William Pitt Byrne memorial fountain. Allan Hume, a founder of the Indian National Congress and known as the father of Indian ornithology, was born on the square. Julia Stephen, mother of Virginia Woolf and Vanessa Bell, lived here. People who died here include the publisher Henry Colburn, the Royal Navy admiral Sir Richard Strachan, known to friends as Sir Dicky, and Henry Waymouth, a founder of the South Australian Company.
